Sibuna 1.0.0-rc.7 adds wildcard host routing and repairs three edges of the PROXY protocol (SID 0036).

- An HTTP route may name a wildcard such as *.example.org, which matches every name under example.org at any depth and not example.org itself, or a list of up to 16 names and wildcards in "hosts". A TLS inspection rule may name a wildcard server name in the same way.
- Sibuna refuses a configuration in which a wildcard hides a later route, a name of a later route or a later SNI rule, and names the earlier route. Files that loaded before load unchanged.
- A TCP pool with proxy_v2 now writes a header for every connection. A client and a listener of different address families no longer close the connection: such a pair is written as IPv6 with the IPv4 address mapped. An IPv4 client on a dual-stack listener is written as IPv4. The PROXY parser reads an IPv4-mapped source as IPv4.
- The health probes of a proxy_v2 pool begin with a version 2 LOCAL header and fail when the server closes the connection at once.
- The operator book explains wildcard routes, and how the health checks of an AWS, Google Cloud or other load balancer in front reach a frontend that requires the PROXY protocol.

TLS 1.3 on the edge, origins and management HTTP paths offers X25519MLKEM768 with classical fallback. SQLx manages the optional PostgreSQL TLS connection separately. Sibuna supports classical certificate signatures with either key exchange.

SHA256SUMS covers the published assets. The OpenBSD package is optional and is attached when its native checks pass.
